_comment: Template for shared/finance/paths.json — copy it, fill in your own paths, and note that the real file is gitignored. This repo is public: the DOMAIN (code, categories, rules) is shared, the WORK (where your statements live, which accounts you have) stays on your machine.

planning_workbook._comment: The top-level planning document. READ ONLY — nothing in this repo ever writes to it. It supplies the categories, the subscription list, the savings rate and the target portfolio.

boat_workbook._comment: Also READ ONLY, and also the best available touchstone: the boat total from the ledger has to match this workbook. If it does not, the parser or the categorisation is wrong — not the bookkeeping.

collect_from._comment: Folders tidy pulls into root, keeping their sub-structure exactly as it is. Left is the source, right the folder name under root.

archive._comment: Superseded material. Moved, not deleted — it may still answer a question later.

context._comment: Prose the author wrote himself: goals, investment strategy, his own summaries. Read as context, never rewritten.

accounts_from_filename._comment: Statement files are sorted into Konten/<account> by what their file name starts with. These prefixes are IBAN fragments and card names, which is why they live here and not in the checked-in domain config.

out_of_scope_targets._comment: Where tidy proposes to move the work folders named in shared/finance.json → tidy.out_of_scope.names. It never touches their contents, and ingest never reads from there.

accounts.label: Commerzbank Girokonto
accounts._comment: dialect names the parser in workflows/finance/statements.py. Never put the IBAN in a file that is not gitignored.
